title: Quarto Template
text:
Preface
This is a Quarto template for lecture material. This template will contain as much of the necessary instructions as possible.
Rendering this document will produce four outputs: html, PDF, docx and epub. All these can be downloaded from the download button on the left. This document will also have a built-in dark mode. The html file will have three possible font styles and sizes for ease of accessibility.

title: 1  General Layout
text:
1.1 Titles
All chapters should start with #. Subsequent headings would start with more #. For cross-referencing, all chapters and sections can be labelled using {#sec-NAME} and then referred to using @sec-NAME. Sections can also be unnumbered by adding {.unnumbered}.
For example, this section is titled ## Title {#sec-Titles} and can be referenced using @sec-Titles to display Section 1.1.

2.2 Font Styles
The three main fonts are italic using *...*, bold using **...** and bold-italic using ***...***.

title: 1  General Layout
text:
2.3 References
The references should all be placed in the references.bib file and laid out in a format similar to BibTex. The references will be displayed in the References chapter in alphabetical order (even the uncited ones) under the Harvard-Bath referencing style (refer to the Harvard-Bath referencing document).
Citations can be made using @ as @Rang2012 and the reference will appear as Rang et al. (2012).

title: 2  Common Usage
text:
2.3 Blocks

2.3.1 Callout Blocks
Callout blocks can be very useful for separating information. Generally, the callout blocks start with :::{.callout-TYPE} and ends with :::. Each callout block style has its own reserved syntax.






Note



Note nte








Warning



Warning wrn








Important



Important imp








Tip



Tip tip








Caution



Caution cau



2.3.1.1 Options
Callout blocks can also have their icons removed with icon=false and be collapsible using collapse=true. By default, the callout box will be collapsible and with an icon.






Caution





Collapsible caution with no icon



Callout boxes can also be titles with ## as the first line of the callout box itself. They can also be labelled with #TYPE-Label and referenced with @TYPE-Label.






Note 2.1: Note Box With Title and Reference



Note with stuff


Note box with label Note 2.1.



2.3.2 Quotes
If there is a specific quote, then Blockquote needs to be used.

Blockquote



2.3.3 Footnotes
Footnotes can also be placed in Quarto using [^LABEL] and the footnote will hover over the clicker1.

title: 2  Common Usage
text:
2.4 Theorems etc.
Theorems, Definitions and such have their own environment. Generally, the callout blocks start with :::{.callout-TYPE} and ends with :::, each one has its own reserved syntax.

Definition 2.1 (Definition) def


Theorem 2.1 (Theorem) thm


Corollary 2.1 (Corollary) cor


Lemma 2.1 (Lemma) lem


Proposition 2.1 (Proposition) prp


Conjecture 2.1 (Conjecture) cnj


Example 2.1 (Example) exm


Exercise 2.1 (Excersise) exr


Solution 2.1 (Solution). sol


Remark 2.1 (Remark). rem

This can be referenced as Theorem 2.1.

title: 2  Common Usage
text:
2.5 Output Specific Formats
Sometimes there are some outputs that will be displayed only for one format only and not others (this is useful when there are moving images or embedded dynamic changes). This can be used using a code block as :::{.content-visible when-format="TYPE" where TYPE is html, pdf or docx.
Things that only appear in HTML version.

title: 2  Common Usage
text:
2.6 Figures
Figures can be inserted using ![Image caption.](figure/directory.png){width=100% fig-align="center" fig-alt="Alternative caption." #fig-FIGURE_LABEL}. All images are clickable and on a lightbox.






Figure 2.1: Image caption here. The image is clickable to enlarge.



Figure can be referenced using @fig-FIGURE_LABEL to give Figure 2.1.

title: 2  Common Usage
text:
2.7 Codes
Some codes can be displayed or executed directly in Quarto. Not every programming language can be executed but Python is one that can be. Executable Python code blocks require {python} but non executable one start with python. Code blocks can also be labelled and captioned with lst-label and lst-cap.




Listing 2.1: Sample caption for code.



Code
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

S = 0

for n in range(1,10):
    S = S+n
    plt.plot(n,S,'.k',ms=10)

print(S)





45









Codes can be referenced using @lst-Sample, like Listing 2.1.

title: 2  Common Usage
text:
2.8 Writing Mathematics
In Quarto, maths can be written exactly as it is written in LaTeX in terms of syntax. Maths can be written in-line using $...$ as \(x=1\), or can be written separately using $$...$$ as \[
x=1.
\]
Equations can also be labelled using #eq-NAME as \[
x=\frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}
\tag{2.1}\] and can be referenced using @ as Equation 2.1.
Many maths shortcuts have been built into the _macros.qmd file.
